lead: three repairers named three reasons for the buzz and each of them was plausible. by the second evening The Root had the instrument in forty pieces on your bench, and the reason was none of theirs.
sun: the repair that would have had it playable by friday gets refused, because a fix that holds is no account of why the failure began. finding that means the thing comes apart to the last joint, and no setting exists on that bench for far enough, so an object arrives whole and wrong and leaves as parts, and the owner is told on the phone that it will be a while yet.
moon: then the maker's hand starts, and most of what goes back is yours: a new bar, a block, a top thinned by your own thumbs at four in the morning. it sounds better than it has in a century, and it goes home under the label glued inside, which carries a name belonging to a man who died two hundred years before you touched it.
pull: the parts holding it up are the parts you made. the name inside belongs to somebody long dead, and no list exists anywhere of how much of the sound is his.
tension: the rattle was supposed to be gone by the weekend. what comes back is correct, honest about eighty years of bad history, and no longer the thing they left. some grieve it in front of you. the collectors stopped ringing years ago, because original material is what they are buying and you will not leave a false cause inside a box to save the wood around it. butchery gets used, and the people saying it have seen the bench.
cost: an instrument nobody could keep in tune for a decade will hold for another hundred years after a fortnight with you, because you went under the three explanations everyone else stopped at. the wood that came off the bench is not the wood that went on. what survives of the man whose name is inside is a label and an outline, and the players are playing you.

lead: the thing you built in a spare room and put on the internet under your name is where nine families finally read what happened to them. the official version had held for twenty years and was the third-best explanation available.
sun: the inquiry stopped where the answer was survivable for people who still had to work together, and that answer was true. under it sat the one that was not survivable, and reaching it meant eleven years of minutes nobody had asked to see. nothing came back at the point where enough had been established. you went down through the version everyone had made their peace with, and nothing of it stands up now.
moon: what came up went out the way it came up. The Jewel puts nothing over a finished thing, so the record is whole, at full length, under one name, no institution behind it, nothing trimmed to make it easier to defend. every step of the reasoning is there to be checked, which is why it is believed and why the people it dismantles have nobody to write to except you.
pull: the true account of it is in public with your name on it and nothing standing in front of it. everyone it takes the ground from under knows exactly where to find you.
tension: it gets used. a campaign lifts one paragraph and drops the qualification on it, a paper wants the angrier version, and no press office sits between any of that and the work, because you never built one and would not know what to staff it with. obsessive is the word that follows you, supplied by readers of the third edition who worked out that you are still down there, which you are.
cost: two of those families got a hearing at all because somebody with no position to protect went below the level the inquiries had agreed to stop at, and came back sourced. the record grows every year, and each edition goes under another person who had settled. it stands in public in your name with nothing over it, and no body anywhere absorbs one part of what comes back at it.

lead: where you are from has a correct answer and nobody else alive is holding it. the name was changed at a port, the village on the certificate is another family's, and the language came in from the other side.
sun: three versions were on offer at home and all three worked: the one about the border, the one about the trade, the one about the uncle who sent for them. going under all three took four years and ended on a single household in a bad decade, findable, with names attached. and no ruling was issued anywhere in you that the kind version had been examined far enough to leave standing.
moon: afterwards there is no room the corrected account puts you in. the relatives carrying the name are still inside the story you took down, the country the papers point at has never heard of you, and neither can be handed the finding. nothing was decided here. the digging left you where it left you, and no part of you objects to the spot.
pull: you know precisely where you came from. it is correct to the household, and it places you on no side, in no country, and among none of the people who share your name.
tension: you get described, kindly, by people who have somewhere, as the one who is not really from anywhere. at a family gathering two relatives introduce you two different ways and both are wrong, and neither can be fixed standing in a hallway. cousins call it disloyal. the part they cannot forgive is the steadiness you came back up with, because the finding took a village off them and appears to have taken nothing off you.
cost: the interest that holds a family story upright was never issued to you, so it came apart in your hands, correctly, with the household at the bottom of it and dates that hold up. what came up out of it fits nowhere. every group that would have claimed you claims on the version you removed, and you are the one person who knows the claim is hollow.

lead: the yard is a trench, the floor is up in three rooms, and eleven years have gone. both reasons the house was failing were real, and each had to be taken to the bottom before either could be believed.
sun: a survey names the likely cause and you cannot use it, because a survey produces the cause that would satisfy a buyer, and a further one sits under that, and reaching it means lifting whatever stands on it. so the ground came up in sections, by hand, each section answering one question and posing the one below it, and no moment came in which the house was declared understood well enough to live in.
moon: The Claws put two live causes under one failure and neither is a hedge. water from above and movement underneath were both doing it, both carrying weight, and settling on one meant building on a half. so the same house got taken apart twice, from two directions, to the same depth, and the second dig could not start until the first was finished, which is where the years went.
pull: two causes, both true, and the only way to be certain of either was to take the house down to it. you were right twice, and nobody has lived in it yet.
tension: your wife wanted a house by the time the children were at school and has had ten years of rented flats and saturdays handing you buckets. two builders told her on the way out that the place had been habitable until you took the yard up. they were right, and what they were describing was a repair. a repair was never what this was, and saying so has stopped sounding like an answer in that kitchen.
cost: hand you a building four people have already explained and you come back with what is happening under it, both halves, in order, and the account will still be right in twenty years. the house you did it to is a shell with excellent drawings. the ones who wanted somewhere to live spent those years elsewhere, and one dig was never going to reach the bottom of it.
